description: ASTRONLION is building BEYOND EARTH, a science-based space survival adventure. Players face Earth's environmental crises, design spacecraft, explore Mars using real NASA data, and make critical survival decisions. Our goal is to turn space science into an exciting interactive experience. We welcome programmers, game developers, AI engineers, scientists, designers, and storytellers worldwide. Join us to explore, discover, and survive beyond Earth!
summary: BEYOND EARTH is an interactive Mars surface mission simulator from team ASTRONLION. After a fictional crisis on Earth, you play a scientist gathering evidence for a future habitat. A 3D map combines NASA Mars Global Surveyor laser altimetry with historical dust conditions reconstructed from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter observations. You compare a direct rover route and a detour by battery use, cumulative ascent and dust exposure, then choose how to reach the science sites. On foot, you scan and collect evidence while keeping enough oxygen to return. You transmit the findings through an orbital relay and test whether a first habitat could sustain a crew for six simulated Martian sols. The prototype makes the trade-offs behind human exploration visible and gives players a way to practice explaining their decisions.
details:
The exploration problem. After a fictional crisis on Earth, the player arrives on Mars as a scientist. The crew must reach useful science sites and bring back evidence with enough energy and oxygen to survive. The prototype follows a fictional traverse in the Schiaparelli region, where players collect clay-mineral evidence and document rock layers to decide where to investigate past water and scout a future habitat.

How it works. The interactive 3D map combines Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) terrain elevation with one historical dust snapshot derived from Mars Climate Sounder (MCS) observations. Players compare a direct route and a detour using estimated energy in watt-hours, cumulative ascent and archived dust exposure. A radio assistant explains the trade-offs using route samples and in-game battery telemetry. The player chooses the route, drives to the science sites, completes an oxygen-limited Marswalk, relays the findings to Earth and tests the habitat’s power, water and oxygen budgets over six simulated sols.

Implementation and educational impact. The browser prototype uses JavaScript, Three.js, Vite and Web Audio, supports keyboard and touch controls, and offers English and Thai. The mission lets learners see how route decisions affect later resource margins. The dust layer represents Martian Year 34, sol 402. Local hazards, waypoints, sample findings, batteries and habitat budgets are simplified for gameplay.

SI disclosure. OpenAI Codex assisted with application code, localization and data-processing scripts. OpenAI image generation supplied illustrative scene artwork that carries a visible watermark. Mission radio clips use eSpeak NG synthetic speech, and the demo uses Kokoro-82M synthetic narration over recorded gameplay. The route model calculates estimates from archived planetary data and in-game telemetry.
